docs.title: Quant Strategies
docs.text:
Backtesting and trading framework for crypto and equity markets. Strategies are built around technical indicators (SMA, EMA, RSI, Bollinger Z-score, Stochastic Oscillator) and optimized via N-dimensional grid search over parameter space.

Target: strategies with Sharpe > 1.5 and strong Calmar ratios.

docs.title: What's Inside
docs.text: Component Description Backtest Pipeline quant/data/sources.py (providers) or MARKET_DATA.PRICE_BAR (exchange venues) → quant/strategy/{indicators,signals}.py → performance.py → optimizer.py → walk_forward.py, orchestrated by quant.cli (CLI) and quant/strategy/backtest_service.py (web, via quant/api/routers/backtest.py) FastAPI Backend REST + SSE for backtest; trade deployments + credentials; REFDATA/instruments — cookie-based auth React Frontend MUI SPA — backtest config/results + Trade UI (accounts, deployments) PostgreSQL Database REFDATA, BT, INST, CORE_ADMIN (users + credentials), TRADE — Liquibase-managed CLI argparse interface for scripted single-symbol backtests and grid searches

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Multi-factor strategies — combine indicators via AND, OR, or FILTER conjunction (web UI)
  • SSE-streamed optimization — real-time progress bar with trial count and best Sharpe
  • Data Column selector — backtest on Price or Volume per factor
  • Walk-forward test — in-sample / out-of-sample overfitting detection
  • Exchange credentials — save, rotate, and revoke broker API keys (Bybit, Binance, Futu) via Trade Config UI
  • REFDATA-driven UI — all dropdowns sourced from PostgreSQL, zero hardcoded lists
  • Authenticated — JWT cookie session; user accounts managed by admin

docs.title: Decisions Log
docs.text:
All agreed design decisions in one place.

# Topic Decision Ref 1 Config split StrategyConfig (backtest identity) + DeploymentConfig (trading target), linked by strategy_id FK. Backtest results stored with strategy for review. design doc §1 2 Conjunction syntax Flat "AND" / "OR" / "FILTER" enum on StrategyConfig.conjunction. No string expression parser. Max 2 substrategies initially. strat.py 3 Substrategy structure Ordered tuple of frozen SubStrategy dataclasses with sequential id. strat.py 4 Optimization config Separate OptimizationConfig, not embedded in substrategy. Runtime args to optimize(). Phase 4 5 Strategy naming Optional name field. Auto-generated as {internal_cusip}_strategy_{id_prefix} if empty. strat.py 6 Multi-factor positions Clean combine_positions() function in strat.py. AND/OR use percentile-rank strength tiebreak. FILTER uses factor 1 as gate, factor 2 for direction. Phase 3 7 Grid search engine Cartesian product as baseline. Bayesian opt via optuna as opt-in alternative. Warn on >10k combos. Phase 4 8 Visualization 1-factor: 2D heatmap. 2-factor: slice heatmaps. 3+: parallel coordinates (Plotly). Phase 5 9 JSON API / DB Full Trade API design doc. Shared DB for backtest + trade. JSON schema for strategy + deployment + backtest results. design doc 10 TypeScript UI FastAPI backend + React/TS frontend. Done — replaced Streamlit. archive/ts-migration.md 11 UUID version UUID v7 (time-ordered) via the uuid7 PyPI package, imported as from uuid_extensions import uuid7. Switch to stdlib uuid.uuid7() when Python 3.14 stable (Oct 2026). strat.py 12 DB naming convention SCHEMA.TABLE format. Schemas: CORE_ADMIN., BT., TRADE., REFDATA., INST.. Columns UPPER_CASE. PKs: <TABLE>_ID. Audit: USER_ID, CREATED_AT always; UPDATED_AT only on genuinely mutable tables (e.g. REFDATA lookups) — soft-versioned tables insert a new row instead of flipping IS_CURRENT_IND + updating. Flags: CHAR(1), no default, no CHECK. DB name: quantdb. No CHECK constraints — validation at app layer. Procedure params: IN_XXX/OUT_XXX. AGENTS.md 13 DB tables BT.STRATEGY, BT.RESULT, TRADE.DEPLOYMENT, TRADE.EXECUTION_EVENT, TRADE.TRANSACTION. No TRADE.INTENT (decision #38). REFDATA.TICKER_MAPPING dropped — replaced by INST.PRODUCT_XREF. design doc §7 14 Ticker mapping ~~REFDATA.TICKER_MAPPING~~ retired. Vendor-symbol mapping now lives in INST.PRODUCT_XREF (one row per product × app). design doc §7 15 Broker adapter pattern TradeAdapter abstract interface. FutuAdapter wraps FutuTrader. DeploymentConfig.broker enum selects adapter. design doc §5 16 AWS infrastructure EC2 t4g.medium (Graviton ARM, ~$14/mo reserved). RDS PostgreSQL 17.9 Serverless v2 (~$5-15/mo). ECR pull deploy via GitHub Actions. Managed via CloudFormation (aws/cfn/<service>/). infrastructure.md, decision #34 17 Local dev DB ~~SQLite or Docker Postgres locally via DB_URL.~~ Superseded — local dev now connects directly to the live Aurora cluster via the AWS SSM port-forward tunnel on localhost:5433 by default. Local Postgres re-introduced as an opt-in via DB_TARGET=local (see decision #30). dev-vs-prod.md 18 Risk checks Kill switch, paper-first default, max position, stop loss, cash check, signal validation, duplicate guard. design doc §4 19 No direct DML All writes via stored procedures (CALL schema.procedure(...)). Liquibase seed changesets are the only exception. AGENTS.md 20 INST schema New INST schema for product master: PRODUCT, PRODUCT_XREF (REFDATA.TICKER_MAPPING dropped), PRODUCT_GRP, PRODUCT_GRP_MEMBER. BT.API_REQUEST gets PRODUCT_GRP_ID + VENDOR_KEY columns (SYMBOL kept until data migration). database.md 21 INTERNAL_CUSIP Stable product identifier on INST.PRODUCT. Always lowercase, format {symbol}.{suffix}. One row per logical instrument — never one row per broker. Bybit, Binance, and other ccxt venues share the same cusip; they differ only in INST.PRODUCT_XREF (VENDOR_SYMBOL per REFDATA.APP id). Crypto spot: suffix .crypto; {symbol} is the quote pair you trade (e.g. btcusdt.crypto for BTC/USDT on Bybit and Binance). Research providers use different vendor strings via xref (BTC-USD on Yahoo, BTC on Glassnode) — do not put broker names or Yahoo tickers in the cusip. Wrong: btcusdt.bybit, btc-usd.crypto when live execution is USDT. Crypto perps: exchange-specific when margin/settlement differs (btc-perp.binance). Listed equity: listing venue (aapl.nyse). INST.PRODUCT.EXCHANGE is for listing/clearing venue on equities — NULL on .crypto spot. Amends the earlier btc-usd.crypto example. INST.PRODUCT, database.md 22 INST versioning PRODUCT uses soft-versioning (PRODUCT_VID + IS_CURRENT_IND). PRODUCT_XREF uses version rows plus transaction-time windows (PRODUCT_XREF_VID, TRANSACT_FROM_TS, TRANSACT_TO_TS). PRODUCT_GRP and PRODUCT_GRP_MEMBER do not — hierarchy versioning is impractical; PRODUCT_GRP uses UPDATED_AT for admin edits, PRODUCT_GRP_MEMBER is add/remove only. database.md 23 PRODUCT_XREF population Long-term design is semi-automatic vendor import with proposal/approval before writing INST.PRODUCT_XREF. Until that workflow exists, admin/bootstrap population may be done directly in the DB. Application write paths still use stored procedures. Amended by #62 — creating a single instrument is no longer a hand-written INSERT; only bulk catalogue seeding still is. separate-underlying.md 24 DbGateway + schema repos (strict-OOP) quant/shared/db.py provides the DbGateway base class — the only module in quant/ that imports psycopg / psycopg_pool. Subclasses call _call_get / _call_write / _query and never touch the driver directly. Amended by #69 — persistent: bool is gone; every call borrows from a process-wide ConnectionPool. No conn= kwargs. RefDataCache (in-process) was superseded by Redis-backed RedisRefData (see decision #31). pipeline.md, db-connections.md 25 Drop TICKER_MAPPING REFDATA.TICKER_MAPPING dropped via Liquibase changeset 116-refdata-drop-ticker-mapping. Functionality replaced by INST.PRODUCT_XREF. No Python code referenced it. database.md 26 Backtest queue infrastructure ~~TypeScript coordinator + Python worker~~ — superseded by decision #32. Postgres-backed FIFO queue with soft-versioned BT.QUEUE (one row per state transition) and BT.SP_INS_QUEUE writes remains; only the language split changed. Original rationale (TS for SSE / type-sharing with frontend) was outweighed by the operational cost of running two services and the duplicated DB-access layer. backtest-queue.md 27 Authentication Cookie-based JWT session (qs_token, HttpOnly, Path=/api, SameSite=Lax). HS256 with JWT_SECRET from SSM (prod) or auto-generated (dev). Login rate-limited via slowapi (5/15min per IP). User accounts admin-managed — no signup endpoint. Argon2id for password hashing. login.md 28 Frontend testing Vitest 4 + React Testing Library + happy-dom. Tests live next to code (*.test.ts(x)). Shared render wrapper at frontend/src/test/wrapper.tsx (provides QueryClient + MUI theme + MemoryRouter). testing.md 29 Client-side routing react-router BrowserRouter (declarative mode). /login → LoginPage (guest-only), / → BacktestPage (auth-required), /* → catch-all redirect to /. Route wrappers RequireAuth / GuestOnly replace the old Gate component. Nginx try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html handles server-side fallback. login.md §9.1, frontend-audit.md 30 Optional local Postgres for dev Decision #17 (SSM tunnel only) is now the default, not the only option. Opt-in DB_TARGET=local switches dev to a host-side Postgres 17 (port 5432) populated by ./scripts/dbctl.sh dump|restore from Aurora. When set, ./scripts/appctl.sh dev start also brings up Redis + the Python queue worker via docker-compose.dev.yml. FastAPI publishes REFDATA into Redis on boot — start the API (or docker compose up api) before the worker so dropdowns populate. Teammates without local PG leave DB_TARGET unset and use the SSM tunnel. dev-vs-prod.md 31 refdata/ separated from data/ quant/refdata/ (Redis-backed config dimensions) is a sibling package of quant/data/ (Postgres-backed time-series + instrument facts), not a subfolder. Different storage tier (Redis vs Postgres), different read/write asymmetry (many readers / one publisher vs per-call read+write), different freshness model (Redis refdata:version and config:version stamps checked on get() vs no version stamp). Boot ordering is enforced by quant/refdata/bundle.py::DataCaches, which constructs RedisRefData first, then InstrumentCache and BacktestCache (which depend on REFDATA for APP_ID / APP_METRIC_ID lookups). quant/refdata/publisher.py is the only Postgres-touching file in refdata/ and the only writer of refdata:* and config:* Redis keys (replaces the former TS coordinator's coordinator/src/refdata/cache.ts). Invoked from FastAPI's lifespan and the admin endpoint POST /api/v1/refdata/refresh. Amended by #44 — quant/data/ is the backtest data tier (BT cache, INST cache, vendor sources); MARKET_DATA.PRICE_BAR is owned by quant/market_data/. bundle.py / publisher.py / reader.py 32 Queue collapsed into Python Done. TypeScript coordinator removed. FastAPI serves /api/v1/backtest/jobs/* (enqueue, list, cancel, SSE). Long-lived quant.queue.worker_loop claims jobs via Redis wake + SP_INS_QUEUE. coordinator/ deleted. backtest-queue.md, quant/api/routers/jobs.py 37 API URL namespaces Backtest: /api/v1/backtest/* + /api/v1/backtest/jobs/*. Shared: /api/v1/refdata/*, /api/v1/inst/*, /api/v1/auth/*. Trade (planned): /api/v1/credentials/*, /api/v1/trade/* (deployments, apply, log). UI mode does not rewrite API paths. api.md, plan-to-profit.md §5.2 33 Live candidate sign-off (Phase 0.1) WATCH for btcusdt.crypto Bollinger momentum 60 / 1.75 (2016-01-01 → 2026-05-16). Full-period Sharpe 1.19; fixed-params OOS (30%) Sharpe 0.42; walk-forward OOS Sharpe negative (overfitting ratio ~1.05–1.09). Promote to Trade picker for dry-run/paper; defer live apply until OOS improves or Phase 2 reconcile confirms edge. Research gate = existing WalkForward / CLI — not production rolling Sharpe. archive/phase-0/phase-0.1-signoff.md 34 Host capacity (Phase 0.2) Prod EC2 upgraded to t4g.medium (4 GiB) for api + worker + redis + future trade worker headroom. YES for Phase 2.2 daily reconcile cron. Capture live: aws/scripts/capacity_snapshot.sh. archive/phase-0/phase-0.2-capacity.md 35 Deploy topology (Phase 0.3) Phase 1: TRADE executor + reconcile cron on same EC2 after t4g.medium upgrade. ECR/CI pull deploy: now — see infrastructure.md § CI/CD. Separate TRADE host: Phase 3.7 only; same ECR repos. Resolves open decision #4. archive/phase-0/phase-0.3-topology.md 36 Exchange API credentials (Phase 1.1) CORE_ADMIN.API_CREDENTIAL only — soft-versioned (API_CREDENTIAL_ID assigned in SP, not table IDENTITY; API_CREDENTIAL_VID on rotate). Broker via APP_ID (REFDATA.APP). Fernet (reversible) + SSM EXCHANGE_SECRETS_KEY — not Argon2/JWT. Reuse auth plumbing (require_user, DbGateway, SP-only writes); do not reuse JWT/Argon2/SESSION_GEN. No TRADE.CONNECTION. TRADE.DEPLOYMENT holds API_CREDENTIAL_ID; trade audit = TRADE.EXECUTION_EVENT / TRANSACTION. API: /api/v1/credentials. plan-to-profit.md §1.1, login.md §6.4, database.md 38 No TRADE.INTENT table Current signal / target action is computed in the trade worker per tick (market orders; pending state is milliseconds). Persist only TRADE.DEPLOYMENT (config), TRADE.EXECUTION_EVENT (submit/error diary), TRADE.TRANSACTION (fills). Revisit a stored “current signal” table only if limit orders or a live-signal UI need state between bar closes — or if multiple strategies net into one order per asset, which needs each strategy's intent recorded separately from the order it contributed to (third trigger, added later; see netting). plan-to-profit.md §1.2, trade-api.md §6 39 BT.STRATEGY temporal versioning Replaced IS_CURRENT_IND with TRANSACT_FROM_TS / TRANSACT_TO_TS (9999-12-31 = active). Column dropped. Liquibase 1.4.0 backfilled from CREATED_AT. database.md 40 IS_BEST_IND promotion model IS_BEST_IND CHAR(1) NOT NULL (no DEFAULT) on BT.STRATEGY. Quality flag separate from temporal versioning. VID 1 = 'Y', VID 2+ = 'N' until promoted. SP_UPD_PROMOTE_STRATEGY flips flag; demote-only when vid=NULL. Worker auto-promotes; manual via POST /strategies/{id}/promote. best-vid-promotion.md 41 REFDATA-driven promotion metrics Auto-promote criteria in REFDATA.PROMOTION_METRIC, not hardcoded. HARD gates (threshold) evaluated first; SOFT metrics (comparison) in priority order. Defaults: Sharpe GT 0 + Max DD LTE 40% (hard); Sharpe, Calmar, returns, drawdown (soft). best-vid-promotion.md 42 Shared strategy pool Superseded on the Trade path. The original rule was a shared pool: any authenticated user could read and deploy any strategy, and USER_ID was audit-only. SP_GET_STRATEGY_LIST now returns only USER_ID = caller, and dry-run / deploy call _assert_strategy_owned (403 otherwise). The promotion log (SP_GET_PROMOTION) is still not owner-filtered. Credential ownership and the paper-vs-live gate are unchanged. user-isolation.md 43 Frontend baseline: Node 24 + React Router 8 + ESLint 10 React Router v8 removed the react-router-dom re-export package, so every import now comes from react-router (declarative mode uses no react-router/dom APIs). v8 requires Node ≥ 22.22 and React ≥ 19.2.7 and ships ESM-only. Node major is pinned to 24 in three places that must stay in sync: .nvmrc, both GitHub workflows, and docker/nginx/Dockerfile (CI and the prod build image were still on 22 while .nvmrc said 24). ESLint 10 was taken at the same time to clear the transitive minimatch/brace-expansion advisory that ESLint 9 pinned. Result: npm audit --audit-level=high exits 0, so the audit gate in both workflows passes. frontend.md 44 market_data/ owns MARKET_DATA end-to-end Every module in quant/data/ is a data-access adapter — two DbGateway caches plus vendor clients — and the orchestration that uses them lives in a domain package (quant/strategy/backtest_service.py consumes BacktestCache; quant/trade/ consumes InstrumentCache). PriceBarService owns the freshness rule, gap repair and the fail-closed decision, so putting it in data/ would mix layers. quant/market_data/ holds repo.py (MARKET_DATA SP wrappers), fetcher.py (public ccxt OHLCV — deliberately not on CcxtTradeGateway, since bars must not depend on a user's API credentials) and service.py (policy), mirroring how quant/trade/ owns TRADE. Interval arithmetic is pure and needed by both bars and the scheduler, so it sits in quant/shared/intervals.py rather than either domain — with no I/O: resolving TM_INTERVAL_ID to a period is RedisRefData.get_interval_period, alongside resolve_app_id / resolve_queue_status_id, so every REFDATA lookup stays in one place. Amends #31. scheduler-price-bars.md, pipeline.md 45 Live signals price off the venue's own bars — venue decides, not schedule Amended by #51 and #80. Dry-run uses the same resolver as live apply (resolve_signal_source), so an exchange venue is priced from PRICE_BAR, not from provider history. A manual apply (no schedule) uses the strategy's fitted interval, not a hardcoded daily. The rest of this row stands: a live apply reads MARKET_DATA.PRICE_BAR from the exchange it executes on whenever that exchange serves market data, manual or scheduled. The schedule only sets the bar interval. The original text said research and dry-run read provider history and that no schedule meant daily via resolve_interval_id(timedelta(days=1)). The provider path survives in live apply only for brokers with no market-data venue (Futu equities), where the provider series is the only one that exists. Consequence: manual and scheduled applies of one deployment read the same series, so attaching a schedule changes cadence, never input data; the fitted-on-provider vs traded-on-exchange divergence applies to all live signals and is traceable via ApplyReport.bar_source. Supersedes the earlier schedule-based switch in LiveApplyOrchestrator._resolve_signal_source. scheduler-price-bars.md, live-trading-promotion.md 46 A missed schedule catches up one interval per pass, at today's price A backlog drains through repeated ticks rather than a jump to the current boundary: ScheduleTickRunner.run_interval advances a due deployment by exactly one interval per pass, reading NEXT_SCHEDULED_TS off the row instead of recomputing from now(), so the schedule keeps its original phase however late the tick ran. Every pass leaves a DEPLOYMENT_SCHEDULE_STATUS row, and that per-slot history is the only record of what downtime cost — collapsing the backlog would reach the same position and erase it. Catch-up does not replay the missed period: load_window derives its window from now(), so each pass computes today's signal and an order fills at today's price. Replay is impossible in principle (an order placed now fills now) and undesirable in practice (a stale signal is worse than a current one), even though load_window(now=...) could reconstruct it and the missed bars are in PRICE_BAR. Repeated applies converge rather than stack, because intended_side compares the signal against the live broker position and returns HOLD once it already matches — so a three-day gap is one trade plus two no-ops. Recovering the P&L of a missed slot is out of scope here and belongs to reconciliation. scheduler-price-bars.md 47 SOURCE_APP_ID belongs in the PRICE_BAR key — a bar is a fact from a venue MARKET_DATA.PRICE_BAR is keyed (INTERNAL_CUSIP, TM_INTERVAL_ID, SOURCE_APP_ID, BAR_TIMESTAMP). Decision #21 makes one product cover a traded pair across brokers, so btcusdt.crypto carries INST.PRODUCT_XREF rows for both Bybit and Binance. Keying without the source let whichever venue wrote a timestamp first own it: the loser's insert raised unique_violation, PriceBarService._insert absorbed it as a benign race, and that deployment priced its signal off the other exchange's prints — while SP_GET_PRICE_BAR_COVERAGE, also unscoped, reported the first venue's bars as the second's freshness so it never even fetched. The result was a silently blended series whose composition depended on which deployment ran first. Both read procedures therefore take IN_SOURCE_APP_ID, and PriceBarRepo / PriceBarService.read_bars require it. This is what lets the table serve as one source of truth for backtest and trade: a paid backfill provider becomes another SOURCE_APP_ID beside live bars rather than a collision, and a backtest pinned to a source reproduces. Prices are not expected to match across sources — separate order books, and provider bars differ again in session convention; the guarantee is consistency within a series, not equality between them. scheduler-price-bars.md §4.1 48 Continuity is repaired explicitly; the live lookback only maintains a rolling window ensure_fresh refills [newest - period × (lookback - 1), newest] and nothing else, and lookback is a bar count (max_window × 3 + 60), so what it covers in wall-clock time depends on the interval: 120 daily bars survive a 10-day outage, 120 hourly bars only five days. Bars older than the window are never requested again, so a longer outage leaves a permanent hole. Trading is unaffected — load_window needs only the window and fails closed if it cannot complete it — but the table is therefore a rolling window maintained as a side effect of trading, not a continuous history, which is not good enough for backtest. PriceBarService.backfill(...) takes an explicit range and fills every hole in it; find_gaps(...) answers the same question read-only. Backfill inverts the fail-closed rule the module otherwise follows: on the trade path a hole must stop the run, but during a repair a hole is ordinary (pre-listing history, or past what the venue retains) and aborting would discard the bars that were recoverable — so it reports BackfillResult.unfilled instead. Separately, catch-up bars are accurate: a closed candle is immutable, so one fetched ten days late is identical to one fetched at the boundary. Depth is bounded by the venue's fetch_ohlcv retention, which is why a paid provider under its own SOURCE_APP_ID (#47) remains the answer for deep history. scheduler-price-bars.md §4.6 49 A deployment may only be scheduled on the cadence its strategy was fitted on Amended by #80 — the allowed cadence is now the strategy's own fitted interval (read from CONFIG_JSON.tm_interval_id), not a platform-wide daily assumption. Decision #45 settled that the schedule sets the bar interval a live signal reads; the consequence is that choosing a cadence is choosing an input series, not a clock. Every backtest fits on daily bars, so the hourly option in the schedule dropdown offered to run daily-fitted parameters over hourly bars. That combination is the worst available failure mode: it is completely silent — a 20-period band computes fine over 20 hourly bars, intended_side returns a real action, the order places, and the execution diary looks healthy, so real money moves on statistics no backtest ever produced and nothing reports a problem. quant/trade/schedule_policy.py now refuses any schedule_tm_interval_id outside schedulable_interval_ids(refdata) with 400 on create and update, naming both cadences; null (manual) always passes, since manual prices off the fitted daily interval. The allowed set is resolved through the REFDATA cache, never hardcoded: the module states the fitted period (FITTED_BAR_PERIOD = timedelta(days=1)) and RedisRefData.resolve_interval_id supplies the id, the same route an unscheduled apply takes under #45 — so a renumbered TM_INTERVAL moves the guard with it, and FITTED_BAR_PERIOD is the single line that widens when multi-interval backtests land. Rendering an interval's name in the rejection is RedisRefData.interval_label() (new, beside resolve_interval_id / get_interval_period), keeping every TM_INTERVAL lookup inside the class that owns the snapshot per #44 rather than letting the trade module read raw rows. Two deliberate edges: an update validates only the value the caller sets, never the stored one, so a row whose cadence predates the rule stays reachable by the kill switch (refusing that PATCH would mean refusing to disable it); and GET /api/v1/trade/schedule-options publishes the set so DeploymentDialog and ScheduleCell grey out the rejected cadences instead of hiding them — a missing option reads as a missing feature, a disabled one plus its helper line teaches that the schedule chooses the bars. scheduler-price-bars.md §3.1.1, api.md 50 Bar capture is subscribable, and a subscription has no owner Amends #5 ("only products with active deployments get bars stored"), which was aimed at avoiding a bulk ingest of every product and was never asked about research. The coupling it created was incidental — bars are public, CcxtBarFetcher is deliberately keyless, and PriceBarService already had sync / backfill / find_gaps / read_bars — so what was missing was a second answer to which instruments matter, not new machinery. MARKET_DATA.BAR_SUBSCRIPTION is that answer: (INTERNAL_CUSIP, TM_INTERVAL_ID, SOURCE_APP_ID), which is PRICE_BAR's key minus BAR_TIMESTAMP, soft-versioned like DEPLOYMENT so the history records which series the platform was capturing when. The motivation is not convenience: #47 §7.7 records live parameters fitted on Glassnode daily data now pricing against Bybit prints, and capturing a venue's bars before committing capital is what lets a strategy be fitted on the series it will actually trade. A subscription is platform-wide, not per user — the design proposed one row per user with a DISTINCT in the warmer, on the grounds that unsubscribing should not stop somebody else's capture; rejected, because a bar is a shared fact and per-user rows model private ownership of something nobody owns. One row per series instead, with UQ_BAR_SUBSCRIPTION_OPEN enforcing it. The table also carries no USER_ID, a deliberate exception to the audit convention of #12: SP_INS_BAR_SUBSCRIPTION still passes IN_USER_ID to CORE_INS_LOG_PROC, so CORE_ADMIN.LOG_PROC_DETAIL answers who changed a series while the version window here answers when — a column would be a second copy of one fact, free to disagree with the log, and no API or UI ever read it. The accepted cost is that disabling stops capture for everyone, which is why the list is unscoped and every row is visible to every signed-in user. Extends #44 to the warm loop: BarWarmer moves from quant/trade/scheduler/warm.py to quant/market_data/warm.py and takes InstrumentSource implementations, because "which instruments matter" stopped being a deployment question the moment it had a second answer. The one-way rule gets stronger — quant/market_data/ knows a protocol, and DeploymentInstrumentSource in quant/trade/bar_source.py supplies the traded half. The two are unioned, not kept in step: auto-subscribing on deploy would force an unanswerable question on every stop (was that capture the deployment's, or wanted in its own right?). Subscriptions are validated on write — product xref present, app resolvable to a ccxt venue — turning three silent per-tick warm failures into one 400. Backfill is exposed as an explicit, reported operation per #48; nothing crawls, and BACKFILL_FROM_TS is intent the UI displays, not progress. The backtest seam that consumes these bars landed as #51. market-data-capture.md 51 A strategy is fitted on the series it will be traded on, and refuses rather than substitute The consequence #50 was built for. fetch_df had one path — getattr(quant.data.sources, app["class_name"]) — and no exchange has such a class, so selecting Bybit as a backtest data source raised AttributeError: module 'quant.data.sources' has no attribute 'Bybit': the one venue a crypto deployment executes on was the one venue it could not be fitted on, and the dialog quietly showed a Yahoo BTC-USD beside a Bybit account. fetch_df now branches on REFDATA.APP.IS_EXCHANGE_IND and reads PriceBarService.read_bars, whose DataFrame is already shape-identical to the provider's, so no indicator or performance code changed. Picking the venue is pinning SOURCE_APP_ID per #47 — no mode flag, no second request field. Three properties are deliberate. The BT.API_REQUEST cache is bypassed, because PRICE_BAR is the store and a copy is a second version of one fact, free to diverge. Nothing crawls: a backtest never triggers a fetch, since capture is a standing decision made on the Market data page per #48, so an uncovered range is an error naming the covered one rather than a five-year exchange crawl on someone's behalf — and never a short series returned under the requested label, which is the silent substitution the whole change exists to end. The daily interval is resolved, not hardcoded: BACKTEST_BAR_PERIOD states the period and REFDATA supplies the id, the route #49 established. Factors keep their own source — the question #50 left open, now closed against live's rule: live routes every symbol to the exchange because mixing series is fatal with capital at risk, while a ^VIX-filtered crypto backtest is legitimate research and no exchange serves ^VIX, so f.data_source or req.data_source stands and a factor inheriting a venue it has no INST.PRODUCT_XREF row on is told to name its own source. Separately, the dry run was fixed to read the live series: it called compute_latest_position without a bar_loader while the apply passed one, so a preview could report HOLD off provider bars and the order that followed BUY off exchange bars, neither malfunctioning. LiveApplyOrchestrator._resolve_signal_source moved to bar_source.resolve_signal_source and both callers share it; a dry run predates its schedule so it falls through to daily, and DryRunReport.bar_source reports the venue beside ApplyReport's. Bybit retains ~6.4 years of BTCUSDT at every timeframe (earliest 2020-03-25), which bounds how far this can be fitted back and is why a deep-history provider under its own SOURCE_APP_ID stays the answer per #48. market-data-capture.md §7 52 A capture range is read from the venue, not typed by the user The gap #50 and #51 left: both dialogs asked how far back do you want history, as a free date field, and nothing knew the answer. Enqueue stays open because the API does not hold the bars. Stochastic's extra warmup and a drawer warning are still open. Stale-row replay, RECIPE_KEY, and the catalog floor in that proposal are not adopted. 2026-09-25-backtest-data-hygiene-proposal.md 79 A failed scheduled apply is retried in the same pass, not on the next tick Amends #70. Its 3-attempt budget was spent one attempt per pass, and the only prod pass is the hourly EventBridge wakeup, so a failed daily apply at 08:05 retried at 09:05 and 10:05 before pausing (visible in EXECUTION_EVENT on 2026-09-22). Each retry traded a signal computed on a bar that had closed hours earlier, at a price the backtest never assumed. ScheduleTickRunner now spends the three attempts inside one pass, DEFAULT_RETRY_BACKOFF_S = 5 apart, and pauses if the last one fails; a reason with requires_operator_fix still pauses on the first. Each retry re-runs the whole apply (connect, bars, signal, fresh position read), so a fill that landed before an error resolves to HOLD rather than a second order. OrderRetryExecutor still retries the order inside each apply. The RETRYING outcome and the in-memory per-SCHEDULED_TS counter are gone, so a restart can no longer reset a count. Trade-off: an outage longer than about 10 s now pauses the deployment for an operator, where the hourly budget could ride out one of up to two hours. That is the intended behaviour: a deployment that missed its bar should be looked at, not traded late. scheduler-trade-open-questions.md

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Copy the template and fill in any keys you need:

cp .env.example .env

The variables below cover the core runtime set. See .env.example for the full template (Cloudflare, Bybit testnet, ECR image tags, and other optional blocks).

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
Variable Required? Description ALPHAVANTAGE_API_KEY Optional Free key from alphavantage.co. Limited to 25 req/day. GLASSNODE_API_KEY Optional On-chain crypto metrics. Only if you use the Glassnode data source. NASDAQ_DATA_LINK_API_KEY Optional Free key from data.nasdaq.com. FUTU_HOST / FUTU_PORT Optional Only if using Futu OpenD gateway for HK/US equities. Default 127.0.0.1:11111.

Note

Yahoo Finance requires no API key — it is the default and recommended data source for getting started.

docs.title: Database (QuantDB on PostgreSQL)
docs.text: Variable Required? Description QUANTDB_HOST Optional PostgreSQL host for the prod target (default: localhost, i.e. the SSM tunnel). QUANTDB_PORT Optional Port for the prod target. Leave unset on a laptop — config/db-targets.json supplies 5433. Setting it to 5432 makes prod point at the local database, which both resolvers refuse. Prod EC2 gets 5432 from SSM together with the real cluster host. QUANTDB_USERNAME Yes Database user. QUANTDB_PASSWORD Yes Database password. QUANTDB_CONNINFO Optional Full libpq connection string. Overrides the four QUANTDB_* vars above. Must include sslmode=require. Use only when you need non-standard libpq options. QUANTDB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT Optional Seconds for Postgres connect_timeout added to the DSN when absent (default: 15). Prevents hung API requests when the tunnel or host is unreachable. PGPASSWORD Optional Mirrors QUANTDB_PASSWORD so psql doesn't prompt interactively.

docs.title: DB target
docs.text:
DB_TARGET selects which of the two databases declared in config/db-targets.json everything connects to — the API, the worker, the CLI, dbctl.sh and Liquibase. Defaults shown below come from that file, not from code; see Dev vs Prod.

Variable Required? Description DB_TARGET Optional local → host-side Postgres 17 on :5432 (no tunnel; dev start also brings up Redis + worker via docker-compose.dev.yml). prod (default if unset) → Aurora on :5433 after ./scripts/appctl.sh prod tunnel start. LOCAL_DB_HOST Optional Overrides the local host (default 127.0.0.1). LOCAL_DB_PORT Optional Overrides the local port (default 5432). LOCAL_DB_NAME Optional Overrides the local database (default quantdb). LOCAL_DB_USER Optional Overrides the local user (default quant_admin). LOCAL_DB_PASSWORD Optional Local user password (default LetsGetRich888 — change for non-default installs). PROD_DB_PORT Optional Overrides the prod port ahead of QUANTDB_PORT. For a tunnel on a non-standard local port. MAX_CONCURRENT_WORKERS Optional Max concurrent backtest worker subprocesses spawned by one quant.queue.worker_loop (default 1; prod sets 2). Safe above 1 — one loop claims sequentially, so the non-atomic claim only races between separate worker_loop replicas, which is what docs/design/backtest-queue.md §0 defers. Bound by cores, not RAM: see Infrastructure Capacity Review §3.2. DB_POOL_MIN Optional Process Postgres pool floor (default 2). DB_POOL_MAX Optional Process Postgres pool cap (default 10). DB_POOL_MAX_IDLE Optional Seconds an extra connection may sit unused before the pool closes it (default 600). DB_POOL_MAX_LIFETIME Optional Seconds after which a connection is discarded on the next checkout (default 1800). DB_POOL_TIMEOUT Optional Seconds to wait for a free pooled connection (default 30).

docs.title: Liquibase (DB migrations)
docs.text: Variable Required? Description LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_URL Yes (for migrations) JDBC URL, e.g. jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5433/quantdb. LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_USERNAME Yes (for migrations) Usually quant_admin for DDL/DML changes. LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_PASSWORD Yes (for migrations) Admin password.

docs.title: FastAPI Backend
docs.text: Variable Required? Description CORS_ORIGINS Optional Comma-separated allowed origins. Not set in code — configure via SSM or .env when the browser hits the API from a different origin than the API itself. Leave unset for same-origin only (e.g. nginx bundle, or Vite proxying /api to the backend). APP_ENV Optional dev (default) or prod. Affects logging, cookie Secure, JWT enforcement. USE_SSM Optional 1 (default in docker-compose.yml) loads secrets from AWS SSM Parameter Store first, then falls back to .env. Set 0 to force .env-only mode. AWS_REGION Optional Region used when USE_SSM=1. Default ap-southeast-1.

docs.title: Authentication (JWT)
docs.text: Variable Required? Description JWT_SECRET Required in prod Symmetric HS256 signing key (generate via openssl rand -base64 32). In dev (APP_ENV != prod) the API auto-generates a random secret each startup. In prod the API refuses to start without it. Rotate by changing the value and restarting. EXCHANGE_SECRETS_KEY Required in prod (Phase 1.1+) Fernet key for encrypting CORE_ADMIN.API_CREDENTIAL ciphertext (python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"). SSM: /quant/prod/EXCHANGE_SECRETS_KEY. Separate from JWT_SECRET. COOKIE_SECURE Optional 1 to force the Secure flag on the auth cookie. Default tracks APP_ENV == prod.

docs.title: Ops alerts (Slack)
docs.text:
Variable Required? Description SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL Optional Incoming Webhook for internal ops alerts (live-apply failures, stale DB connections, …). Messages are prefixed with a searchable category tag ([TRADE], [DB], … — see AlertCategory in quant/shared/notify.py). If unset, alerts are logged only. Use a test channel in dev; prod ops channel only after the pipeline checklist in Live Trading Promotion.

User accounts are admin-managed — there is no signup endpoint. See Login & Authentication for the provisioning flow.

docs.title: Exchange egress
docs.text: Variable Required? Description CCXT_EGRESS_<EXCHANGE_ID> Optional Extra egress routes for keyed ccxt sessions to that venue, named for the ccxt exchange id (CCXT_EGRESS_BYBIT, CCXT_EGRESS_BINANCEUSDM). The format is comma-separated name=proxy_url, e.g. uk=http://13.43.55.53:3128. direct is always tried as well and cannot be redefined; malformed entries are logged and skipped. Each key is routed to whichever route the venue accepts, and the result is cached in Redis. Unset or blank means direct only. Keyless sessions (venue limits, market data) ignore it. Prod: /quant/prod/CCXT_EGRESS_BYBIT. See Infrastructure: Per-key routing.

docs.title: Frontend (Vite dev server)
docs.text: Variable Required? Description VITE_API_URL Optional Backend base URL the Vite dev proxy forwards /api to. Default http://localhost:8000.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Warning

Never commit .env to version control. It is gitignored. Production secrets live in AWS SSM Parameter Store (/quant/prod/*).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text: Requirement Notes Python 3.12+ Used by setup.sh → env/ Node.js 24+ Installed by setup.sh from .nvmrc Git Clone the repo Linux / macOS / WSL Bash scripts below AWS CLI + SSO Shared prod DB (default) and prod Liquibase deploy Docker + Compose v2 Local queue worker (DB_TARGET=local) or appctl prod Java 17+ Liquibase — installed automatically by deploy/verify scripts PostgreSQL 17 Only for a local DB copy (DB_TARGET=local)

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/alfred1123/Quant_Strategies.git
cd Quant_Strategies
cp .env.example .env   # fill in keys — ask admin for DB password / AWS access
./setup.sh             # Python venv + npm install

docs.title: Scripts at a glance
docs.text:
Script Purpose setup.sh Create env/, install Python + frontend deps scripts/appctl.sh Start/stop dev (uvicorn + Vite) or prod (Docker Compose). prod tunnel is the laptop → Aurora forward on :5433 scripts/dbctl.sh Dump/restore/reset local Postgres (:5432) scripts/liquibase-deploy.sh Apply pending DB migrations scripts/liquibase-verify.sh Dry-run: validate changelogs, preview SQL (no apply)

Admin / debug helpers (see Login): scripts/hash_password.py, scripts/diag_login.py.

docs.title: Run the app (dev)
docs.text:
scripts/appctl.sh first argument is how the app runs (dev = uvicorn + Vite on the laptop; prod = Docker Compose). It is not which database you talk to.

Local/dev does not need a tunnel. DB_TARGET=local uses Postgres on :5432.

Prod Aurora from a laptop is a different command: the SSM port-forward on :5433. That is prod tunnel, not dev start.

docs.title: Option A — Local DB (no tunnel)
docs.text:
Offline (or isolated) dev on localhost:5432 with a local backtest queue. Requires Docker for Redis + worker. See Database dump & restore for the first dump.

# in .env: DB_TARGET=local
./scripts/appctl.sh dev start          # uvicorn + vite + docker-compose.dev.yml

Open http://localhost:5173 (API: http://localhost:8000).

A dump from Aurora (one-time) does need the prod tunnel — that is Option B's command, used only for dbctl dump.

docs.title: Option B — Prod Aurora from the laptop (prod tunnel)
docs.text:
Uses Aurora through SSM on localhost:5433. The laptop is not on the VPC; the forward goes through the prod EC2 jump host. AWS SSO must be valid. dev start still runs uvicorn/Vite; it does not start this tunnel.

aws sso login --profile alfcheun
./scripts/appctl.sh prod tunnel start
pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433

# in .env: DB_TARGET=prod  (or leave DB_TARGET unset)
./scripts/appctl.sh dev start

# First-time local copy: tunnel, then dump, then switch to Option A
./scripts/appctl.sh prod tunnel start
./scripts/dbctl.sh reset
./scripts/dbctl.sh dump
./scripts/dbctl.sh restore
./scripts/dbctl.sh bootstrap-roles
# then set DB_TARGET=local and use Option A — no tunnel after that

docs.title: Database migrations (Liquibase)
docs.text:
Schema changes live under db/liquidbase/. Use DB_TARGET to pick the port (see Environment variables):

Target Port When DB_TARGET=local :5432 Local Postgres after dbctl restore DB_TARGET=prod (default) :5433 Aurora via prod tunnel (./scripts/appctl.sh prod tunnel start) 
# Preview pending changes (safe — does not apply)
./scripts/liquibase-verify.sh --offline   # XML parse only
DB_TARGET=local ./scripts/liquibase-verify.sh

# Apply pending migrations
DB_TARGET=local ./scripts/liquibase-deploy.sh

# Prod schema (Aurora) — GitHub Actions → **database** workflow (verify or deploy)
# Or: bash aws/scripts/liquibase-ssm-run.sh verify main

# Prod Aurora from the laptop (prod tunnel on :5433 must be up)
./scripts/appctl.sh prod tunnel start
PROD_DB_PORT=5433 APP_ENV=prod USE_SSM=1 ./scripts/liquibase-verify.sh
PROD_DB_PORT=5433 APP_ENV=prod USE_SSM=1 ./scripts/liquibase-deploy.sh

After a fresh local restore, always run deploy so procs/constraints match source:

DB_TARGET=local ./scripts/liquibase-deploy.sh

Local port override

An explicit DB_TARGET always wins over LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_URL. If .env sets LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_URL=…:5433 and you run DB_TARGET=local, the script uses the local target URL — a shell-exported URL that contradicts DB_TARGET makes the script exit with a conflict error. To aim at a custom URL without a target, leave DB_TARGET unset and set LIQUIBASE_COMMAND_URL directly.

Compare live DB vs source DDL: .github/skills/extractddl/extract_ddl.sh → diff against db/liquidbase/ (see Database).

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
Mode Command What runs Dev support stack ./scripts/appctl.sh dev start with DB_TARGET=local redis + worker from docker-compose.dev.yml Prod stack (local smoke test) ./scripts/appctl.sh prod start docker-compose.yml + docker-compose.prod.yml — nginx, api, worker, redis Prod stack (EC2) Deploy pipeline / aws/scripts/ec2-deploy.sh Same compose files on the server

Dev support stack only — when not using appctl:

docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d        # redis + worker
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml logs -f worker
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml down

Prod stack logs:

docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f

docs.title: Day-to-day commands
docs.text:
Command Purpose ./scripts/appctl.sh dev status Backend, frontend, tunnel, DB, dev Docker stack ./scripts/appctl.sh dev stop Graceful shutdown ./scripts/appctl.sh dev kill Force stop everything ./scripts/appctl.sh dev restart Stop + start ./scripts/appctl.sh prod status Production compose containers ./scripts/dbctl.sh status Local Postgres + latest dump ./scripts/dbctl.sh psql Shell into local quantdb

Logs: log/backend.log, log/frontend.log, log/tunnel.log.

Open http://localhost:8001.
